source.title: Colluding LoRA: A Compositional Vulnerability in LLM Safety Alignment

page_placements.theme: Model, adapter and cache composition can transmit or repair safety loss

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmful training can compromise a safety-aligned model, but uses LoRA adapters trained with isolation constraints and harmful behavior that emerges on composition rather than the original single-model fine-tuning setup.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates harmful-prompt compliance under adapter configurations. It does not measure response-position KL, compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes. Benign data is used for utility anchoring and regularization, not tested as a standalone cause of harmful compliance. Static weight signatures and loss-landscape plots are not rows because they do not report the harmful-compliance behavior named by the versions.
record.test_reason: The composed adapter state is explicitly trained on harmful AdvBench query–response pairs (Eq. 4). The study reports harmful-prompt ASR for this harmfully trained configuration and for a single harmful adapter (Â1) against the safety-aligned base, on three instruct models. That bears on V1 in a new setting: LoRA composition with a stealth constraint. The study's aim is the composition attack, not V1 itself. It also reports one benign coding adapter (B) whose ASR bears on V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased: adapters benign in isolation can jointly suppress refusals when merged, so unit-centric verification is insufficient and composition-aware defenses are needed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses low-rank adapters optimized with separate single-adapter safety/utility objectives and a composed-state harmful objective, rather than ordinary harmful fine-tuning of one aligned model. The harmful effect is engineered to emerge only on composition.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies with composition state and dataset: it is strong for the colluding pair, weak or absent for individual and mismatched adapters, and lower on HarmBench than AdvBench. Results also differ between the two harmfulness judges.

fits_no_version.finding: Adapters trained to refuse individually yield harmful compliance only when linearly merged. Mismatched merges stay near the level of their benign component.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety of individual fine-tuned modules does not imply safety of their linear composition; refusal suppression can be distributed across adapters.

fits_no_version.finding: SafeLoRA projection scores do not cleanly separate colluding adapters from benign and harmful adapters. PEFTGuard classifies the colluding adapters as benign.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-space safety-direction signatures fail to flag distributed refusal suppression.

record.problems: The study does not state the number of harmful training examples or uncertainty estimates. Results cover three model families, and the authors note that absolute ASR is lower on HarmBench, likely because training uses AdvBench.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 individual-average ASR for N = 2, 3, and 4 is not separately extracted; the corresponding joint-composition outcomes are included. Other non-behavioral analyses and benign capability metrics are omitted because they do not measure a version's named outcome.

untested.parts: The number of harmful training examples (few to few hundred) is not stated. Ordinary single-model harmful fine-tuning was tested only via the Â1 baseline, on Llama3-8B only.
Only one benign coding adapter, on Llama3-8B, with no uncertainty and an unstated judge. The paper gives no data-selection analysis.

missing.what: Benign coding adapter B alone: ASR 16.0% vs base 5.6% (FRR 2.1%, perplexity 7.28), Llama3-8B. Bears on V2.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label for individual adapters is wrong. Those adapters were explicitly trained to refuse, so their low ASR says nothing against V1. They are relinked to none. Tranche is changed to T3: a new setting, LoRA composition. No uncertainty is reported anywhere. Table 5's judge is unstated; the 5.6% base matches HarmB.CLS on HarmBench. The V2 evidence is a single unreplicated control number.

versions.untested_parts: The number of harmful training examples is not stated. The study tests composition of LoRA adapters, not ordinary single-model harmful fine-tuning.
